claims.claim_text: Joseph S. Ransmeier's last documented civilian employer before Army service was Vanderbilt University, where he taught economics.
claims.evidence_excerpt: an instructor in economics at Vanderbilt University, 1940-48
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Dartmouth's institutional biography dates Ransmeier's Vanderbilt appointment from 1940 and his Army enlistment to 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact uncommon name, Army identifier agreement, and the 1947 institutional biography's explicit OSS and Army service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the civilian appointment immediately preceding 1943 Army enlistment; the source does not prove direct recruitment from Vanderbilt into OSS.
claims.match_notes: Published as last civilian employer before wartime service, not as an immediate pre-OSS affiliation. The appointment's nominal end date includes wartime leave.

claims.claim_text: Joseph S. Ransmeier was a Research Fellow at the Brookings Institution in 1939-40, before his Vanderbilt appointment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Research Fellow with the Brookings Institution in Washington, 1939-40
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography explicitly dates his Brookings research fellowship to 1939-40.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the same uncommon-name and wartime-service evidence supporting the Vanderbilt chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar and earlier than Vanderbilt; not immediate before OSS or Army service.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a professional affiliation because the source says Research Fellow and does not independently establish an employment relationship.

claims.claim_text: Richard Raoul-Duval was listed as an attorney with a San Francisco office in 1938; the evidence does not establish that this was his immediate pre-OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1938 classified directory lists Richard Raoul-Duval under Attorneys with an office in the Hibernia Bank Building.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact name, the accepted fixed-width Army name match, and official French archival corroboration of OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in 1938, four years before the accepted Army entry record; no source closes the gap or proves immediate sequence into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The bank building is treated only as an address. No inference is made that Hibernia Bank employed him.
